_: FILM 6 -- The Monkeys Who Watered the Garden (jataka-more).
THE PRIMITIVE IS `world`, and it is the counterpart to film three's `rock`. `rock` promised
the world STAYED THE SAME across a film -- the same stone, the same waterline, every night.
This promises the opposite and just as strictly: the garden CHANGES, in one declared
direction, and never drifts back. Get it wrong and no single shot is wrong; a kept garden
in shot 12 looks perfectly fine on its own, and only the film is broken.
So the stages are film-level and ORDERED, in rig.world, and a garden shot writes
"world": "uprooted"
INSTEAD of a plate. A shot cannot name both, so it cannot show a stage that is not one of
these four, and film.js checks that the sequence never runs backwards and that the first
and last stage both appear -- a garden of wilted sticks is only a loss to a viewer who was
shown the kept one. Shots that are not in the garden name a plate as usual: the mango tree
is not a stage of the garden.
AND THE PLATES ARE MEASURED NOW, not asked. Each stage names the one before it as its
canonical composition, and film.js correlates their edge maps: on the plates already in
this repo a canon-matched pair scores 0.64-0.96 and two different places 0.10-0.17, so a
stage that quietly came back re-framed is caught before a frame is rendered. Prose has
failed at this twice (film three's rivers, film four's yard) and both times a person had
to notice.
CAST: the monkey is free. THE GARDENER IS THE CHANNEL'S FIRST HUMAN -- see
cast/gardener/cast.json, and read it before publishing anything he is in.
